gaps.construct: reflect.Type as a map key and the input to newTypeEncoder
gaps.description: The doc has no type-as-value and no way to inspect a value's type at run time; the key is declared as an opaque TypeDescription with no source.

gaps.construct: encoderFunc func values stored in a map, plus an anonymous func literal that captures `indirect`
gaps.description: No function type, no lambda, no capture and no way to call a stored operation; `Operation from ... to nothing`, `operation given ... doing` and `call f with ...` are invented.

gaps.construct: sync.OnceValue: a value computed once on first use, safely shared by racing goroutines
gaps.description: No lazy or once-only value exists; `once ... computing` and `value_of` are invented.

gaps.construct: package-level encoderCache (sync.Map) shared and mutated by all goroutines
gaps.description: The doc forbids sharing mutable values between tasks (example 38) and shows no module-level var; the cache was turned into a capability parameter, changing the public signature of typeEncoder and pushing the parameter onto every caller.

gaps.construct: deliberately racy publication protocol: LoadOrStore of a placeholder, then Store of the real encoder, with other goroutines briefly using the placeholder
gaps.description: Structured concurrency with no shared mutation cannot express a benign race between independent callers; the translation is correct only for one caller at a time.

gaps.construct: (value, ok) two-result lookup and (actual, loaded) from LoadOrStore
gaps.description: Mapped to `maybe EncoderFunc` with `choose`; works cleanly but LoadOrStore's two meanings of the result (found vs stored) live only in a note.

gaps.construct: an arm of `choose` that does nothing and falls through
gaps.description: The doc does not say whether an empty `when` arm is allowed; only an empty `on failure` is forbidden.

gaps.construct: type assertion fi.(encoderFunc) on an any value from sync.Map
gaps.description: Absorbed by typing the cache as holding EncoderFunc; the doc has no generic map type, so EncoderCache is opaque.

doc_rules_contradicted: Because values are never shared mutably between tasks, there is nothing for a lock to protect, and no way to forget one.
invented_syntax: Operation from A and B and C to nothing
operation given a, b and c doing
call f with a, b and c
notes: This is the canonical memoised-recursive-builder pattern (cache + placeholder to break cycles) and it needs four things Scribe lacks at once: reflection, first-class functions, lazy once-values and a shared concurrent cache. The capability model also has no story for a process-wide cache that is semantically pure (a memo), so threading it as `uses encoder_cache` makes every JSON encode look effectful.
